mechanism: A one-millisecond aligned timer grid for both BackToBackBeginFrameSource users can reduce redundant frame/ack CPU under classic uncapped scheduling without dropping demand or acknowledgements. Existing 500us timer judder guard implies nominal 0.5–1.5ms rearm wait, not a strict 1ms interval. First delivery also waits; metadata continues to use vsync/max-VRR interval.
switch: FLASHWRIGHT_PACED_UNCAPPED_FRAMES=1; default off; native getenv only in constructor

scope.workload: Unchanged original setup body, 15 tests per preflight capture and 240 per timed capture including warmup-labelled tests. Every original semantic observation and expected fixture request count verifies.
scope.reference: Same newly built custom browser with switch off/on; no Playwright run in this screen.
scope.policy: Existing renderer reuse, classic early-idle/uncapped scheduling, lazy VAAPI discovery and locator cache off. Original public launch arguments preserved before explicit private feature additions. Four-core quota, CPUs0–5, 8 GiB, swap0, Nice10.
scope.timing: Complete watchdog-owned fixture/runner/browser interval including natural drain; inner owner elapsed and cgroup CPU/peak memory also retained. No sampling or timing instrumentation in browser.
scope.controls: Both arms pass three fresh storage/global contexts, real-time moving-target actionability with trusted clicks, finite nondecreasing self-chained rAF timestamps, screenshot dimensions and exact pixels, live timer progress and observed idle CPU. Broader scheduling correctness remains unverified.

advancementRule: Require all functional controls, at least 10% lower complete setup time in both blocks at each worker count and at least 20% lower charged CPU in both four-worker blocks. Otherwise restore baseline without application expansion. Passing screen would require original TodoMVC/SVGOMG and broader lifecycle/artifact controls before any adoption.

decision.reason: Both one-worker elapsed reductions are below 10%. Four-worker elapsed and CPU gates pass in both blocks.
decision.nextEvidenceNeeded: The CPU benefit under parallel contention motivates a separate demand-aware scheduling hypothesis. It does not justify adopting this fixed delay or changing its predeclared gate.

restoration.build: Original file bytes restored with new mtime; native incremental build completed and reproduced exact baseline executable hash. No active candidate remains.

buildCorrection: Initial compilation rejected unchecked C-string indexing under Chromium unsafe-buffer diagnostics. Replaced it with std::string_view equality before any candidate execution. Retain original failed build; no workload retry.
limitations: Two reversed blocks per worker count, without confidence intervals. Setup scaling is diagnostic and does not replace the original nine-scenario final matrix.
The one-millisecond grid delays requested and first frames too. Existing 500us alignment guard means nominal 0.5–1.5ms rearm delay, plus scheduling; two source layers may each wait.

Begin-frame interval/deadline metadata still use existing vsync/max-VRR values. GPU availability callbacks can bypass a fresh paced wait. This is not a guaranteed 1000Hz display or strict minimum delay.
No changes to frame-demand predicates or no-damage acknowledgements; unchanged action ordering does not prove all renderer lifecycle semantics.
